Check a SatGate receipt
You can check a SatGate receipt here in a few seconds, without taking our word for it.
Why it matters

A receipt records what your agent asked for and what SatGate decided. Your agent never writes or edits its own record. Because anyone can check a receipt, you can hand one to an accountant, an auditor or a customer, and they can confirm it for themselves.
Check one in three steps
In your SatGate dashboard, open Activity, pick an entry and choose Download. You get a small file called an Evidence Pack. It holds the signed receipt.
Drop the file on the box below.
Read the result. Valid means SatGate signed this receipt and what it signed hasn't changed since. Not valid means don't rely on it.
Drop a receipt file here, or choose one
Your file stays on your computer. The check runs in your browser and nothing is uploaded.
What gets a receipt

SatGate signs a receipt when it refuses an agent over a budget, a missing payment or a permission, and when an agent spends from a budget in Control mode, where SatGate enforces your limits. If SatGate can't make the receipt, the request is still stopped.
Not every request gets a receipt. A refusal for going over a rate limit doesn't get one, and neither does a request that never goes through SatGate.
A receipt shows which tool or service your agent called, whether SatGate allowed or refused it, and a refusal code. It doesn't name the agent or include what the agent sent.
What a valid receipt doesn't show
It shows what SatGate decided. It doesn't show what happened after SatGate let a request through, for example whether a broker filled an order or whether a payment settled.

Limits
Anyone with a pack's link can open that pack until it's deleted, so share links with care.
Our signing keys are kept in our hosting provider's secret storage, not in a hardware security module, and they haven't had an outside security assessment.
Receipts are stored in SatGate's own storage. Nothing outside SatGate anchors them, so keep your own copy of any receipt you rely on.
A valid check shows the receipt is intact and was signed with SatGate's key. It doesn't show what an outside service did, whether money settled, or that you meet any regulation.
